axes.function_family: what the sound DOES in a track
axes.source_attributes: provenance tags, NOT classes (foley, weather, vinyl, ...)

principles: A class must name ONE thing. Negative silhouette means it names several.
Provenance is an ATTRIBUTE, not a class. Foley describes where a sound came from, not what it does; splitting it acoustically manufactures structure that is not there.
Other/none is REJECTION material. Its heterogeneity is intended and it must never be asked to form a compact prototype, nor be an auto-rename target.
Definitions cite measurable physics where measurement supports them, so a human and the model can agree on a boundary.

Kick.definition: Low-frequency drum hit, fundamental typically 50-120 Hz, fast attack, dominant energy below 200 Hz.

Snare.definition: Mid-band drum hit with noise component from snare wires, fundamental typically 180-350 Hz.

Clap.definition: Multi-burst noise transient, little harmonic content, energy concentrated 1-4 kHz.

Hi-Hat.definition: Short bright metallic transient, very high zero-crossing rate, negligible low end.

Crash.definition: Metallic cymbal with long bright decay, broad bandwidth, single onset.

Rimshot.definition: Sharp stick-on-rim crack, instant attack, very short decay.

Percussion.definition: PARENT CLASS ONLY - not a leaf. Measured incoherent; use a subtype.

Tom.definition: Pitched drum with real low end. The only percussion subtype with substantial energy below 200 Hz.

Shaker/Tambourine.definition: Bright rattling noise, essentially no low end, high zero-crossing rate.

Hand Drum.definition: Conga, bongo, djembe and related. Did not emerge as a separate cluster - too few examples. Provisional. NOT OBSERVED in the owner sprint - no examples produced.

Other Percussive Hit.definition: Instant attack, gone within ~60 ms, low harmonicity. A crack rather than a tone.

Unsure.definition: Reviewer could not place it. Kept explicitly rather than guessed.

Metallic.definition: Bell, chime, metallic strike. Distinct ring and long bright decay.

Foley.definition: PROVENANCE label, not an acoustic class. Recorded real-world object. Do NOT split acoustically - measured clusters are weak (0.103) and that is the correct result for a provenance label.

Percussion Loop.definition: Repeating percussion pattern. Measured incoherent - contains at least bright/noisy (shaker, hat, top) and low/tonal (conga, hand drum) groups.

Drum Fill.definition: Non-repeating transitional drum phrase. Distinct from a loop: it does not repeat.

Bass Reese.definition: SUSTAINED detuned-saw bass. Long sustain, high harmonicity. The most acoustically coherent class in the corpus.

Bass Hit.definition: Fast-attack low-sustain bass hit. Distinct from Bass Reese on the envelope axis despite few examples.

Synth One-Shot.definition: Measured to contain THREE groups, only one of which is a one-shot. Should be split by envelope into Synth Pluck (short, fast attack) and Synth Tone/Pad (sustained). Duration separates them at d-prime 2.47.

SFX.definition: Designed sound effect. Measured incoherent - a catch-all.

Impact.definition: Large low-frequency hit used for emphasis.

Weather/Nature Atmos.definition: RECORDED atmosphere (rain, wind). NOTE: this is a provenance distinction from Atmosphere, not a functional one - consider migrating to a source attribute.

Foley Loop.definition: Repeating recorded real-world pattern. Provenance label, see Foley.

Other/none.definition: REJECTION material. Not an acoustic class, never an auto-rename target. Heterogeneity is intended and expected; negative silhouette here is correct.

impulse_response.rule: Files under an impulse-response directory are flagged is_impulse_response=true and EXCLUDED from the default train/eval split.
impulse_response.rationale: An impulse response is a measurement of a space, not a musical sample. The product would never usefully rename one. They are the worst-performing collection (12.5%). Labels are RETAINED, never deleted, so the decision is reversible.
